free_text: The patient is a 70-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 8.4 ng/mL and a prior biopsy showing Gleason 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1). MRI demonstrated a PI-RADS 4 lesion (cT1c) without extracapsular extension. The management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefit of treatment against the risks associated with the current low-grade disease and patient preferences.
